_source.Study Title: Transcriptional analysis of kidneys from mice flown on the RR-7 mission

_source.Study Protocol Description:
Twenty (20) mice (female, 10 C57BL/6J mice and 10 C3H/HeJ mice, ~11 weeks of age at launch) were launched in one Transporter and transferred to two Rodent Habitats without dividers onboard the International Space Station (ISS). In the Transporter, the C57 mice were housed on one side of the unit and the C3H were housed on the other side, with a wire grid divider separating the two sides and strains. Each strain was then housed in its own Habitat for the remainder of the study.   Half of the mice from each strain (5) were maintained in microgravity for ~25 days before being euthanized, scanned using Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA), and dissected on the ISS (Timepoint 1 group), while the other half were maintained in microgravity for a total of ~75 days before euthanasia, DEXA scan, and dissection (Timepoint 2 group).  The Baseline, Vivarium, and Ground Control groups were all maintained, euthanized, and dissected at Kennedy Space Center (KSC). Ground Control and Vivarium animals were euthanized and dissected at 2 Timepoints, mimicking treatment of Flight animals.  The study followed recommendations in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and the protocol (Protocol number RR7) was approved on Dec. 14, 2017 by the NASA Flight Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).

RR-7 Ground Control Rerun Experiment: Preliminary behavioral analysis data from the RR-7 mice in 2019 suggested that results obtained from the Ground Control group were not consistent with previous findings that sleep/wake rhythms are more disrupted in flight. Further investigation into the RR-7 experiment revealed that not all of the Rodent Habitats used for the RR-7 experiment were equipped with the same LED lighting: the two Ground Control units had blue-enriched LEDs whereas the two Flight units had the standard white LEDs. One of the original central hypotheses tested in RR-7 was that disruption of sleep and circadian rhythms in spaceflight augments spaceflight-induced disturbances in other systems (i.e. microbiome and metabolism). Previous studies also indicated that light spectrums can influence the expression of circadian behavioral rhythms. Without exactly matched LED light spectrums for the in-flight versus ground control habitats, the PIs could not confidently attribute RR-7 flight vs. ground behavioral and molecular differences as being due to spaceflight. Thus, no meaningful conclusions could be reached from the RR-7 experiment.
On April 16, 2020, a request was made to the Ames Space Biology Control Board (ASBCB) to repeat the Ground Control portion of the RR-7 experiment at KSC with LED light spectrums exactly matched to habitats flown in RR-7 (2 white, 2 blue-enriched LED, 40 mice). This request was granted and scheduled for Spring 2021 due to conflicts with hardware availability, facility availability, and the COVID-19 pandemic. The RR-7 GC Rerun experiment ran from March to June 2021, mimicking the original RR-7 Ground Control timeline and procedures. The 40 mice (20 C57Bl/6J (B6) and 20 C3H/HeJ (HeJ) female mice, ~11 weeks old) were “launched” on March 22, 2021 and maintained in either white or blue-enriched LED containing Habitats for up to 25-26 days (known as experiment day “30”) or 75-76 days (known as experiment day “90”).
Mice underwent DEXA scans, fecal collections, and weight measurements using the Mass Measurement Device (MMD). Not all mice were weighed– during the original RR-7 flight experiment, 5 mice from each strain were randomly chosen to be weighed at timepoint 1 instead of all 10 per strain due to time constraints. The B6 mice were dissected on April 16 and June 6, 2021, and the HeJ mice were dissected on April 17 and June 5, 2021, all during the hours of 8:45-13:35 GMT (during the lights on period 05:00-17:00 GMT).
Each mouse was anesthetized and imaged with a bone density scanner, followed by exsanguination via cardiac puncture. Each animal was dissected for PI tissue collection (left liver lobe, gastrointestinal tract, spleen) and the remaining carcass was sectioned into three parts (head, chest, and abdomen/hindlimbs), preserved in RNAlater, refrigerated at +4C for ~72 hours, and then stored at -80C for further dissection.     All of the mice were euthanized by intraperitoneal injection of Ketamine/xylazine/acepromazine. Liver, gastronitestinal tract, and spleen were collected followed by carcass sectioning into 3 sections, head, chest, and abdomen with tail removed and discarded.Carcass sections were submerged and preserved in RNAlater, refrigerated at 4C for ~72 hrs, and the frozen at ~-95C. All tissue samples and sectioned carcasses were returned to earth on SpaceX-16 on January 13, 2019 and delivered to Northwestern University for final dissection.  Baseline, Vivarium, and Ground Control samples were shipped to Northwestern University at three different times (late-July, mid-September, and late-September 2018). Dissections for tissues from all experimental groups were completed at Northwestern University by the PI groups along with NASA's Biospecimen Sharing Program in February 2019. All kidney tissues used for extraction in this dataset were preserved in RNAlater after dissection and stored at -80C. The frozen preserved tissues were shipped frozen to NASA Ames Research Center and handled by LSDA.

The RR-7 GC Rerun BSP dissections were performed at Northwestern University, July 26-30, 2021, in which the BSP Team coordinated and performed an integrated dissection with the PI Team, managed by Co-I Dr. Martha Vitaterna. Dissections were performed on two days: July 28 and 29, 2021, 20 mice each day. The frozen, RNAlater-preserved Head, Chest, and Abdomen sections were transferred from -80C to +4C the day before each dissection to thaw overnight (carcass sections for mice  1-20 thawed for ~20-26 hrs, and carcass sections for mice  21-40 thawed for ~17-22 hrs). On each dissection day, the Head, Chest, and Abdomen vials were transferred out of the +4C refrigerator. Dissected samples including kidney were kept at -80C freezer until processing.     RNA was extracted using the AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Valencia, CA). Homogenization buffer for RNA purification was made by adding 1:100 beta-mercaptoethanol to Buffer RLT (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) and kept on ice until use. Approximately 20 mg of frozen tissue was isolated using a scalpel, weighed and immediately placed in 600 uL of the Buffer RLT solution. Homogenization was performed using tissue homogenizing bead mix (Navy RINO Lysis, Next Advance) on Bullet Blender Gold 24 (Next Advance) for 3 minutes at 4C. Homogenates were centrifuged for 3 minutes at RT and 14,000 g to remove cell debris. The supernatant from each sample was then used to isolate and purify RNA following the manufacturer protocol. RNA was eluted in 50 uL RNAse free H2O. Concentration for all RNA samples were measured using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) with Qubit RNA BR kit. RNA quality was assessed using the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer with the Agilent RNA 6000 Nano Kit (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA).

For Ground Control Rerun samples: RNA was extracted using the AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) following GeneLab SOP 3.1-Qiagen AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini with Qiagen RNase-Free DNase set. Homogenization buffer for RNA purification was made by adding 1:100 beta-mercaptoethanol to Buffer RLT (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) and kept on ice until use. Approximately 20 mg of tissue was isolated using a scalpel, weighed, and immediately placed in 700 uL of the Buffer RLT solution. Homogenization was performed using tissue homogenizing bead mix navy, (Next Advance, Raymertown, NY) on Bullet Blender Gold 24 (Next Advance, Raymertown, NY) for 3 minutes at 4C per SOP 2.1-Tissue homogenization Using Bullet Blender Gold Bead Beater. Homogenates were centrifuged for 5 minutes at RT and 14,000 g to remove cell debris. The supernatant from each sample was then used to isolate and purify DNA and RNA following the manufacturer protocol. RNA was eluted in 50 uL RNAse free H2O, and DNA was eluted in 50 uL RNAse free H2O. Concentration for all RNA samples were measured using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) with Qubit RNA BR kit following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter. RNA quality was assessed using the Agilent 4200 TapeStation with the Agilent RNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). DNA quality and size were assessed using the Agilent 4200 TapeStation with Agilent gDNA ScreenTape Kit (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.     ERCC ExFold RNA Spike-In Mixes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA Cat   4456739, v92) at 1:100 dilution of either Mix 1 or Mix 2 were added on the day of library prep at the concentrations suggested by the manufacturer protocol.

For Ground Control Rerun samples: ERCC ExFold RNA Spike-In Mixes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, Cat 4456739, v92), Mix 1 or Mix 2, were added on the day of library prep at the concentrations suggested by the manufacturer protocol. SOP 5.2 Use of ERCC Spike-In Mixes and UMRR/UHRR Controls for Total RNA Sequencing. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.     RNA ribo depletion was done with Illumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Library Prep Gold (Illumina, San Diego, CA). Input RNA were approximately 500 ng with RIN greater than 4. Index adapters were 1.5 uM (IDT, 384-well xGen Dual Index UMI Adapters). 15 cycles PCR were performed. Library fragment size ~300 bp was assessed using Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 DNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). Pooled library concentration was measured by Universal qPCR Master Mix (Kapa Biosystems, Wilmington, MA). Library quality control was determined by iSeq100 (Illumina, San Diego, CA).

For Ground Control Rerun samples: RNA ribo depletion and library preparation was done with Illumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Library Prep Gold (Illumina Inc., San Diego, CA) following GeneLab SOP 5.1 Ilumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Lirary Prep using epMotion. Input RNA were approximately 500 ng with RIN greater than 4. Index adapters used were at 1.5 uM (IDT, 384-well xGen Dual Index UMI Adapters). 15 cycles PCR were performed. Library fragment size was assessed using Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 DNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA) following GeneLab SOP 6.3 Quality analysis of sequencing libraries using 4200 TapeStation System with D1000 reagent kit. Pooled library concentration was measured by Qubit 4 Fluorometer (ThermoFisher Scentific, Waltham, MA) following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter. Library quality assessment was performed on iSeq100 (Illumina, San Diego, CA). Universal mouse reference RNA (Cat 7500600 Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA) was included in the library preparation as a positive control. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.     RNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Paired end 98bp. PhiX included as control.

For Ground Control Rerun samples: RNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Sequencing was set up as following: Read 1: 151 bp, Index1: 17 bp, Index2: 8 bp, Read 2: 151 bp. PhiX v3 was included as control and to increase library diversity. Protocol followed is SOP 7.1-Setting up NovaSeq 6000 and iSeq 100 Sequencers. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.     UMIs were extracted from fastq files using UMI-tools v1.1.0 (v1.1.2 for GC rerun samples). Quality assessment of reads was performed with FastQC v0.12.1 and reports were combined with MultiQC v.126. rRNA percentages of reads were estimated with the 'hts_SeqScreener' program of HTStream v.1.1.0 (v1.3.2 for GC rerun samples) screened against a fasta file of M. musculus rRNA sequences retrieved from NCBI on 09-2019 (05-2025 for GC rerun samples).     Data were processed as described in GL-DPPD-7101-G (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/master/RNAseq/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7101_Versions/GL-DPPD-7101-G.md), using NF_RCP version 2.1.0 (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_RNASeq_Workflow/tree/NF_RCP_2.1.0). In short, raw fastq files were filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10) powered by Cutadapt (version 4.2). Trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Mus Musculus STAR and RSEM references were built using STAR (version 2.7.11b) and RSEM (version 1.3.3), respectively, Ensembl release 112, genome assembly GRCm39 (Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa) concatenated with ERCC92.fa from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip), and the following gtf annotation file: Mus_musculus.GRCm39.112.gtf concatenated with the ERCC92.gtf file from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip). Trimmed reads were aligned to the Mus Musculus + ERCC STAR reference with STAR (version 2.7.11b) and alignment log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). Aligned reads were assessed for strandedness using RSeQC infer_experiment.py (version 5.0.4), gene body coverage using RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py (version 5.0.4), inner distance was assessed using RSeQC inner_distance.py (version 5.0.4), and distribution of RNA features using RSeQC read_distribution.py (version 5.0.4). Aligned reads from all samples were quantified using RSEM (version 1.3.3), with strandedness set to forward and RSEM count log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). To create a set of rRNA-removed quantification data, Ensembl IDs mapping to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) were removed from the RSEM gene count data. Both the original set of RSEM quantification data and the rRNA-removed data were subject to differential gene expression analysis as follows. A runsheet was generated with dp_tools (version 1.3.8) and the runsheet and quantification data were imported to R (version 4.4.2) with tximport (version 1.34.0), ERCC genes were removed, and the non-ERCC genes were normalized with DESeq2 (version 1.46.0) median of ratios method. Normalized gene counts were subject to differential expression analysis. Differential expression analysis was performed in R (version 4.4.2) using DESeq2 (version 1.46.0); all groups were compared pairwise using the Wald test and the likelihood ratio test was used to generate the F statistic p-value. Gene annotations were assigned using the custom annotation tables generated in-house as detailed in GL-DPPD-7110-A (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/GL_RefAnnotTable-A_1.1.0/GeneLab_Reference_Annotations/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7110_Versions/GL-DPPD-7110-A/GL-DPPD-7110-A.md), with STRINGdb (version 2.16.4), PANTHER.db (version 1.0.12), and org.Mm.eg.db (version 3.19.1). Assessment of ERCC spiked genes was performed as detailed in the ERCC_analysis_GLbulkRNAseq.html report.
_source.Study Description: The objective of the Rodent Research-7 mission (RR-7) was to study the impact of the space environment on the gut microbiota of two strains of mice and how any changes in-turn affect the immune system, metabolic system, and circadian or daily rhythms. To this end, ten 11-week-old female C57BL/6J and ten 11-week-old female C3H/HeJ mice were flown to the International Space Station on June 29, 2018 on SpaceX-15 and housed in two Rodent Habitats. Samples of food, swabs from living surfaces, and fecal pellets were collected from each animal before launch and regularly during the mission. The mission also involved extended video collection (48 hr video segments per Habitat) to monitor circadian rhythms, and on-orbit mass measurement. After 25 days on-orbit, half of the mice of each strain were euthanized on the ISS with Ketamine/Xylazine/Acepromazine and cardiac puncture, after which carcasses were segmented in three sections and preserved in RNA later. After 75-76 days the remaining 5 animals from each group were euthanized and processed in the same manner. The 25-day dissected carcasses returned on SpX-15, and the 75-day dissected carcasses returned on SpX-16. In addition to the Flight group, three ground control groups were also part of the study: Basal (representing the pre-launch state), Vivarium (standard vivarium housing for the same duration of time as flight), and Ground (same habitat in the International Space Station Environment Simulator, ISSES). Twenty mice (10 of each strain) were included in each of these control groups, which were euthanized and processed on the same schedule and in the same manner as the flight samples. Dissections for tissues from all experimental groups were completed by the PI groups along with NASA's Biospecimen Sharing Program in February 2019. GeneLab received kidneys from thirty-eight C57BL/6J mice: 9 Basal, 5 Ground (25 days), 4 Ground (75 days), 5 Flight (25 days), 5 Flight (75 days), 5 Vivarium (25 days), 5 Vivarium (75 days). GeneLab received kidneys from thirty-nine C3H/HeJ mice: 9 Basal, 5 Ground (25 days), 5 Ground (75 days), 5 Flight (25 days), 5 Flight (75 days), 5 Vivarium (25 days), 5 Vivarium (75 days). From these kidneys, RNA was extracted, libraries generated (stranded, ribodepleted) and sequenced (target 60 M clusters at PE 98 bp). Since the original RR-7 experiment used different wavelengths of light in the Spaceflight (FLT) and Ground Control (GC) Habitat units (the two GC units had blue-enriched LEDs whereas the two FLT units had the standard white LEDs), the GC was repeated for RR-7 on 07/28/2021 - 07/29/2021 such that mice were exposed to either blue or white light. The GC rerun samples can be compared to the data from the original RR-7 samples to evaluate any biology impact due to exposure to different wavelengths of light.

all: Space Station on June 29, 2018 on SpaceX-15 and housed in two Rodent Habitats.
